scope: Production ScriptHost outer executor before/after; actual CoreCLR C# Vector128 W1/W3 over authoritative module ECS columns. Not a Unity comparison.
change: One-system outer schedules run on caller while row jobs retain parallel execution; independent multiple systems retain multithreaded execution. Zero-worker outer schedule uses sequential execution. Original Bevy zero-worker executor already polled global tasks; this is not a deadlock fix.
quality: 20actualCLR1003-row smoke cases pass including baselinezero-worker, scalar/span/SIMD, Release/hot, fullIDs/componentpresence/every12floatbit and507W3bouncedrows.15integrationtests pass: final deferred writes, queryrefresh,1->2->1reloads/livehandles/state, zero-workers, host, modules, spans and sparse views. Focusedclippy and formatting pass; independent schedule/FFI review no remainingmustfix.
method: Two fresh reversed rounds, same14pool+caller theoretical15runner budget,1mrows, W1warm120/W3warm3000,300samples. Setup/compile/spawn/validation/dumps excluded; same .NETprebuilt bytes and benchmark source in pairedbuild. Guarded before/after and2s snapshots, exact runenvironment retained. Resource monitor filters common compiler names; it is not continuous scheduling isolation or a full process-tree profiler.
limits: Median gains small/mixed (~1-5%) and tails vary; not a20% engine-speedup claim. New actual C# cross-engine comparisons are a separate profile. Windows/NativeAOT execution not covered. Two zero-worker paths both complete; prior deadlock concern corrected.
